nackt.et: From Middle High German nacket, from Old High German nackut, from Proto-Germanic *nakwadaz, from Proto-Indo-European *nogʷós (“naked, bare”). Cognate with Low German naakd, Dutch naakt, English naked, Danish nøgen, Swedish naken.

Nacken.et: From Middle High German nacke, from Old High German *hnahho, from Proto-West Germanic *hnakkō, from Proto-Germanic *hnakkō (“nape, neck”), from Proto-Indo-European *knog-, *kneg- (“back of the head, nape, neck”).

nackig.et: Alteration of now archaic nackicht, itself an alteration of Middle High German nacket.

s: a blow, usually a slap, on the nape of the neck
a shock, blow, something unexpected that causes setback or demoralisation
Nackenschlag.et: From Nacken (“nape of the neck”) + Schlag (“blow”).

Nacktbaden.et: nackt (“naked”) + Baden (“bathing”), gerund of baden (“to bathe”).
